items.title: NASA images reveal crater left by SpaceX rocket's Moon crash
items.summary: WASHINGTON: NASA on Tuesday released new images of the crater caused by a SpaceX rocket slamming into the Moon earlier this month. The photographs were captured by the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) between August 11 and 12, and show the impact formed by a SpaceX Falcon 9 upper stage striking the Moon's surface on August 5. The LRO, in service since 2009, circles the Moon from pole to pole every two hours while the Moon rotates underneath it.

items.title: US targets Iranian hackers accused of stealing 31.5TB of data
items.summary: NEW YORK: US authorities expanded its prosecution of a sprawling Iranian hacking network Tuesday, bringing to 17 the number of indicted suspects for an alleged campaign against universities, companies, and government agencies. The Department of Justice unveiled a new indictment targeting eight additional individuals, with nine of the 17 defendants having already been indicted in 2018. The expanded case now covers the hacking of 144 US universities and 178 foreign universities, as well as at least 42 US companies, 11 foreign firms, five US government agencies, and two NGOs.

items.title: Govt open to GST features in SST as experts see potential to plug tax gaps
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The government is open to incorporating selected Goods and Services Tax (GST) features into the existing Sales and Service Tax (SST) to strengthen revenue collection without imposing a broad-based tax on Malaysians already facing cost-of-living pressures. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said SST would remain the basis of the tax system, but the government could consider features that improved its efficiency and revenue collection. "GST is a broad-based tax that taxes everyone.

items.title: 'Meticulous planning' behind brazen Genting jewellery robbery [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The speed in which three robbery suspects made off with almost RM1.7 million worth of jewellery at SkyAvenue, Genting Highlands, coupled with their escape from the police dragnet, suggests the heist may have involved a degree of planning. Senior lecturer and criminologist at Universiti Malaya Dr Haezreena Begum Abdul Hamid said the fact the robbers could carry out the robbery indicated that they might have familiarised themselves with the location. The fact that they could carry out the robbery and escape with almost RM1.7 million in jewellery within two minutes suggests a high level of confidence and, quite possibly, prior planning.

items.title: UUCA explained: Malaysia’s 55-year-old campus control law and the repeal now on the table
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — The Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (UUCA) is set to be repealed, marking the end of a contentious 55-year legal era that defined, and often stifled, student activism in Malaysia. The road to restriction The UUCA was Malaysia’s answer to a wave of student unrest in the early-to-mid 1970s, when university students were among the country’s most vocal critics of poverty and inequality. The UUCA was tightened to curtail student activism following the Baling incident in December 1974.

items.title: Trump, Carney hold last-minute talks ahead of new Canada tariffs
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney held urgent talks with US President Donald Trump on Tuesday, hours before fresh US tariffs on Canadian goods were set to come into force. Trump signed orders for the steep 50-per cent duties last month, with the White House alleging "discriminatory treatment" by Canada against US alcohol, automobile and dairy products. A White House official said any deal announcement would come directly from Trump.

items.title: UAE accuses Iran of targeting shipping with ballistic missiles
items.summary: DUBAI: The United Arab Emirates on Tuesday accused Iran of firing two ballistic missiles at shipping in the Gulf, an allegation later denied by Teheran. "UAE air defences detected two ballistic missiles launched from Iran toward the country, with the first falling outside the country's territorial waters, while the second fell within the territorial waters," the ministry said, in a statement posted to social media. The first UAE statement came nearly two hours after a brief phone alert warned residents of a "potential missile threat."

items.title: 'Potential contracts worth RM39.6b missed over 3 years'
items.summary: PROJECT opportunities worth RM39.59 billion have been missed over three years due to the small number of facility management contractors, said Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Maslan. He said the Construction Industry Development Board (CIDB) recorded 1,541 facility management and maintenance projects between 2023 and 2025 but there were only 468 contractors registered under the F01 and F02 facility management specialisations. He said facility management received less attention as contractors and the industry traditionally focused on construction, with maintenance regarded as a secondary activity.

items.title: 'Most content flagged for removal is on Facebook'
items.summary: He said 78 per cent of online gambling content requested for removal was on Facebook, followed by 18 per cent on YouTube and four per cent on TikTok. For scam content, Facebook topped the list at 53 per cent, followed by TikTok at 39 per cent and Threads at five per cent. "Of the total requests to remove criminal content, 91 per cent involved online gambling content and scams.

items.title: Israel blames Turkiye after strike on Syrian air base
items.summary: The strike marks extraordinary defiance by Israel of the United States, which has sought to support Syria's new government led by a former jihadist allied with Turkiye. "Israel and Syria agreed to a status quo in security matters, which Syria was on the verge of breaching by permitting Turkish troops to deploy at an airbase near Aleppo," Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office said in a statement after a day of official silence by Israel. "Israel repeatedly warned Syria that such a deployment would pose a threat to Israel's security.

items.title: Online job listings fall 11.4pc in Q2
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The number of online job offerings advertised fell 11.4 per cent to 555,509 in the second quarter of this year from 626,816 in the preceding quarter, the Statistics Department said. Professionals accounted for the largest share of online job offerings at 51.5 per cent, or 285,907 positions, down 9.5 per cent from 315,768 in the previous quarter. Managers followed with 87,950 job offerings, while technicians and associate professionals recorded 86,512.

items.title: Lula hails new oil find as 'passport to the future'
items.summary: BRAZILIAN President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on Monday hailed the discovery of oil near the Amazon coast as a "passport to the future", despite strong opposition to drilling in the area from environmentalists. Oil giant Petrobras last week announced it had identified the presence of hydrocarbons off the coast of northern Amapa state, nearly a year after it began drilling. The discovery is "a passport to this country's future and in saying this, I'm not denying my fight to one day be free of fossil fuels", Lula declared on a visit to Petrobras' operations base, dressed in one of the company's orange jumpsuits.

items.title: Trump claims Hormuz as 'new US territory', denies Iran talks
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said Tuesday that no talks with Iran are underway and none are scheduled, as he posted a map showing the Strait of Hormuz as a new American territory in a fresh jibe at Tehran. "The Hormuz Strait is open and operating. Iran, however, denied firing a missile toward the UAE.

items.title: Foreign borrowers banking on Asia-Pacific bond markets
items.summary: In fact, "kangaroo" bond sales from foreign issuers in Australian dollars are at a record high of around A$60 billion so far this year, up roughly 40 per cent from last year, the London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG) data tracking internationally placed deals up to late last month shows. Chinese onshore "panda" and offshore "dim sum" yuan bond sales reached record highs of around 160 billion yuan and 350 billion yuan, respectively, in the first half, rising more than 60 per cent compared to this time last year, according to Goldman Sachs, with half of it coming from international borrowers. Global international syndicated bond sales this year reached a record above US$4 trillion by late last month, according to LSEG, from around US$3.5 trillion in the same period last year.

items.title: Backlash after Thailand frees 85-year-old drug trafficker
items.summary: BANGKOK: Thailand's justice minister pledged on Tuesday to review pardon criteria following backlash over the release of an 85-year-old drug trafficker who served less than a decade of a life prison sentence. Laota Saenlee, a former anti-communist guerrilla turned drug runner linked to powerful Myanmar drug kingpins, was arrested by undercover officers in 2016 for selling crystal meth in the Golden Triangle drug-producing region. Thailand's corrections department said Monday that Laota was released from a maximum-security prison just north of the capital Bangkok on Friday following a series of royal pardons that reduced his life sentence to below the nearly 10 years he served.

items.title: Khalil Al-Hayya, the Hamas chief who met Kushner
items.summary: KHALIL Al-Hayya, the Hamas chief who met United States envoy Jared Kushner, President Donald Trump's son-in-law, in Cairo on Sunday, emerged as a pivotal figure in the Palestinian group during the Gaza war as Israel killed its other leaders. Named Hamas' overall leader last month, Hayya narrowly escaped assassination himself in an Israeli air strike in Qatar last year that killed his son and aides. Born in the Gaza Strip in 1960, Hayya joined the Muslim Brotherhood movement from which Hamas emerged in 1987.

items.title: UN says only 3 per cent of Gaza cropland accessible and undamaged
items.summary: ROME: Just three per cent of the cropland in Gaza remains accessible and undamaged, the UN's Food and Agriculture Organisation warned Tuesday, citing an analysis of satellite images. The report found that since October 2025, when a fragile ceasefire between Israel and Hamas took hold, the area of accessible and undamaged cropland had fallen to 448 hectares from 601 hectares, a reduction of 25.5 per cent. Greenhouse availability has also declined, dropping 17.3 per cent since October 2025 to 224 hectares that are accessible and undamaged.

items.title: NST Leader: Reinventing road safety
items.summary: ROAD accidents cause up to RM30 billion in socio-economic losses, Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi disclosed on Monday. Road accidents impose costs far beyond the immediate loss of life or damage to vehicles. RM30 billion is a staggering annual economic loss.

items.title: Fitness coach dies after collapsing during Hyrox event
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A Thailand-based fitness coach died after he collapsed and lost consciousness during a Hyrox event in Bangkok last Thursday. The Bangkok Post reported that Leroy Saunders, a 41-year-old South African, was resuscitated and taken to hospital after collapsing during the Hyrox Bangkok 2026 event at the Queen Sirikit National Convention Center. According to the report, Saunders owned IAOT CrossFit in Bangkok, and was known for strength and conditioning work with combat athletes.

items.title: Israeli airstrikes hit Syrian airbase, draws condemnation
items.summary: DAMASCUS/ ANKARA: Israel bombed an airbase in Syria on Tuesday, Syrian state media said, carrying out what appeared to be its first strike on Syrian government assets since March and drawing condemnation from Turkey and criticism from a US envoy who called it an "unnecessary escalation." Syria's state-run Ekhbariya, citing a military source, said Israel carried out eight airstrikes on the runway and storage facilities at the Abu al-Duhur base, while a separate military source and a civilian who lives near the base said there were no casualties. Israel has repeatedly struck Syrian forces since Assad was ousted in 2024.

items.title: Report: Govt withdraws appeal against court ruling on liquid nicotine
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government has reportedly withdrawn its appeal against a High Court decision in May that overturned the move to remove liquid nicotine from the list of scheduled poisons. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad and the government had previously been reported to have filed an appeal against the Kuala Lumpur High Court's decision on May 15, which ruled that the health minister's decision to remove liquid nicotine used in vape and electronic cigarette products from the list of poisons was irrational and made without proper consultation with the Poisons Board. The court found that the decision to remove liquid nicotine used in vape and electronic cigarette products from the Poison List was ultra vires (beyond the legal powers conferred by law) Section 6 of the Poisons Act 1952.

items.title: Trump posts map showing Strait of Hormuz as US territory
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Tuesday posted a map on his Truth Social platform showing the Strait of Hormuz as "NEW U.S. Trump first raised the idea of a US takeover on Friday, saying in a jovial-sounding tone he would soon declare it to be US territory -- prompting Iran to retort that the strait "will remain Iranian." Before the Iran war erupted on February 28, the Strait of Hormuz was an open, international waterway.

items.title: 7 cleaning workers to be nominated for state honours
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: Seven recipients of this year's Cleaning Workers Award will be nominated for state honours (Pingat Kebaktian) from their respective state rulers. "This year's Cleaning Workers Award recipients will be nominated to the respective state palaces to receive state meritorious service medals from their state rulers," he said during his speech at the Cleaning Workers Day appreciation ceremony here today. Nga said Penang had already set a precedent in honouring cleaning workers, and urged other states to adopt a similar approach.

items.title: Syed Saddiq, Bella Astillah to wed on 10.10.26 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Muar member of parliament Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman and his fiancée, Bella Astillah, have announced that they will tie the knot at Level 118 of the Menara Merdeka Maybank here on Oct 10. Syed Saddiq, 34, and Bella, 32, who got engaged on March 28, also announced that their wedding would adopt an all-white theme infused with Arab or Islamic elements, at the request of their families. The video showed Syed Saddiq and Bella walking together before revealing their wedding date at the end, generating excitement among viewers.

items.title: Malaysia could experience 'Super El Nino' from Oct, hottest weather since 1997-98
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The likelihood of El Nino, which typically brings hotter and drier conditions, reaching the 'very strong' or 'Super El Nino' category between Oct and Dec has risen to more than 90 per cent. Mohd Hisham said current global climate patterns indicated that the 2026–2027 El Nino could rank among the most extreme events ever recorded, with its impact potentially exceeding or at least matching that of the very strong El Nino episodes in 1997-1998 and 2015-2016. Mohd Hisham said the strong El Nino was also expected to occur alongside a positive Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD), potentially intensifying the reduction in rainfall across the region.

items.title: 14,807 littering notices issued, 548 ordered to perform community service
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: A total of 14,807 notices were issued to litterbugs, with 548 people ordered to perform community service in states enforcing the Solid Waste Management and Public Cleansing Act 2007. Six states have adopted the Act, namely Johor, Melaka, Negri Sembilan, Kedah, Perlis and Pahang, along with the Federal Territories. To date, 15 rounds of the Community Service Order programme have been conducted, totalling 2,279 hours of community service since the law took effect on Jan 1.

items.title: 2 KPDN officers injured during LPG enforcement operation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Two Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) enforcement officers in Selangor were injured while carrying out their duties under Ops Tiris 4.0, an operation to curb the misappropriation of subsidised liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) through decanting activities. Its Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said assistant enforcement officer Mohammad Fauzi Baharuddin sustained fairly serious injuries and was still receiving treatment. He said another enforcement officer R. Yoghanath sustained minor injuries.

items.title: Trump says no talks taking place with Iran, maintains Strait of Hormuz is 'open'
items.summary: WASHINGTON: United States President Donald Trump on Tuesday said there were no conversations taking place with Iran, and none were scheduled, adding that the Strait of Hormuz was open. The Hormuz Strait is open and operating. Top Iranian negotiator Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf said in comments published by state media on Tuesday that the Strait would remain shut until the US met the conditions of an interim deal signed with Iran in June.

items.title: Syndicate repackaging subsidised cooking oil as prayer oil busted
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry in Kuala Lumpur has busted a syndicate misappropriating subsidised packet cooking oil by repackaging and selling it as prayer oil in four raids in the capital today. The ministry's Kuala Lumpur deputy director Mohd Shahran Mohd Arshad said the operation under Ops Tiris 4.0 uncovered three interlinked cases and seized nine tonnes of cooking oil worth about RM165,000. "For one premise alone, an estimated 200 bottles or nearly one tonne of subsidised cooking oil were processed daily.

items.title: Thailand to overhaul gun control - Deputy PM
items.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Pakorn Nilpraphunt said the current system needs to be completely modernised, with tighter inspections, stronger oversight, and the closing of existing loopholes. Pakorn said the current system relies heavily on manual records, making it difficult to track licences. He also said no new firearm approvals would be issued at present.

items.title: Sarawak eyes direct Kuching–Jeju flights as AirBorneo expands regional tourism links
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 18 — Sarawak is seeking to establish direct AirBorneo Airways (AirBorneo) connectivity between Kuching and Jeju Island in South Korea as the state moves to expand access to key regional tourism markets. Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Minister Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah said South Korea was among the markets being considered for AirBorneo, with Jeju Island identified for the proposed direct connection. Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Minister Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah said South Korea was among the markets being considered for AirBorneo, with Jeju Island identified for the proposed direct connection.

items.title: Kuala Pilah school lab roof collapse prompts chemical removal, JKR to assess safety
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, Aug 18 — The roof of a laboratory at Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan (SMK) Juasseh here suddenly collapsed at noon today. Kuala Pilah Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Operations Commander, Senior Fire Officer Mohd Idham Mohd Rodzi said no casualties were reported in the incident. — Bernama

items.title: 1MDB civil trial: Shahrol Azral denies Jho Low acted as PM, insists Najib briefed indirectly
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 18 — Former 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) chief executive officer (CEO) Datuk Shahrol Azral Ibrahim Halmi told the High Court today that he did not “treat” fugitive businessman Low Taek Jho, or Jho Low, as the country’s Prime Minister. Shahrol Azral: Yes. They named former prime minister Najib, 1MDB’s former finance director Terrence Geh Choh Heng, former executive director Casey Tang Keng Chee, former general counsel Jasmine Loo Ai Swan, Vincent Beng, former chief financial officer Radhi Mohamad, Kelvin Tan, and former chief investment officer Nik Faisal Ariff Kamil, as defendants.

items.title: Heavy rain, strong winds forecast in multiple states, MetMalaysia issues evening alert
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 18 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds across several areas in Peninsular Malaysia until 9pm today. In a statement, it said the affected areas include the whole of Perlis and several districts in Kedah, namely Langkawi, Kubang Pasu, Kota Setar, Pokok Sena, Padang Terap, Yan and Pendang. A similar warning has also been issued for several areas in Perak (Kuala Kangsar, Hulu Perak, Selama, Larut Matang and Kerian); Kelantan (Tanah Merah, Machang, Pasir Mas, Kota Bharu and Tumpat); Pahang (Maran, Rompin, Pekan and Kuantan); and Johor (Johor Bahru).

items.title: Court adjourns Pulau Batu Puteh appeal, Dr Mahathir’s lawyer seeks to add RCI report
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 18 — The Court of Appeal here today adjourned the hearing of former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad’s appeal after his lawyer indicated that he would file an application to adduce the Pulau Batu Puteh Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report as fresh evidence in the appeal. The three-member bench comprising Datuk Azizul Azmi Adnan, Datuk Ong Chee Kwan and Datuk Seri Mohd Radzi Harun allowed Dr Mahathir’s lawyer, Zainur Zakaria, two weeks to file the application. He said when the High Court judge decided on his client’s judicial review application, the RCI report was not available.

items.title: Sabah Fire Dept issues stern warning as eight areas hit by 12‑day dry spell
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 18 — Eight areas across seven districts in Sabah are experiencing a prolonged dry spell, with between 12 and 14 consecutive days without rain recorded as of yesterday. He said Keningau and Pitas recorded the longest dry spell, at 14 consecutive days, followed by the Wario Livestock Centre in Kota Belud and Ranau Station, at 13 days each. He added that four other locations — the Kimanis Agriculture Office in Papar, Laban Rata at Mount Kinabalu in Ranau, Serinsim Sub-Station in Kota Marudu and Kota Kinabalu Station — had recorded 12 consecutive days without rainfall.

items.title: High Court to deliver Aug 24 ruling on Negeri Sembilan Undang eviction summons
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 18 — The High Court today set Aug 24 for its decision on an originating summons filed by the Negeri Sembilan state government seeking an immediate eviction order for the official halls and residences of the Undang Rembau and Undang Sungei Ujong. The Negeri Sembilan state government filed separate originating summonses against Abdul Rahim and Mubarak on 16 and 17 July, respectively. Besides Abdul Rahim and Mubarak, other respondents named include occupants or individuals residing at the official halls and residences of Undang Rembau and Undang Sungei Ujong.

items.title: ‘Who wants power forever?’: Azalina confirms PM term limit bill retabled in October
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 18 — The bill to cap the prime minister’s tenure to a maximum of 10 years will be retabled during the next Parliament sitting in October, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said confirmed today. When asked if the government could secure a two-thirds majority for the bill, Azalina briefly said: “Looks good. Who wants power forever?”

items.title: Malaysia, Philippines discuss swift repatriation of 5,000 undocumented migrants detained in Sabah depots
items.summary: MANILA, Aug 18 — Malaysia and the Philippines today discussed measures to expedite the repatriation of more than 5,000 undocumented Philippine migrants held at four immigration depot centres in Sabah. Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said screening by the Philippine Embassy in Kuala Lumpur identified over 1,000 individuals ready for immediate deportation. Mohamad said both nations also discussed educational provisions for the undocumented migrants’ children in Sabah.

items.title: MRT Corp announces Aug 20–Oct 31 lane closures for Penang’s Mutiara Line construction
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 18 — Periodic partial lane closures along Jalan Tun Dr Awang and Jalan Dato Ismail Hashim, from the Sri Relau Complex to the Penang Golf Club, near here, will be implemented from Aug 20 to Oct 31 to facilitate preliminary construction works of the Mutiara Line Light Rail Transit (LRT) project in the area. “The closures involve several lanes, including the right lane of Jalan Dato Ismail Hashim, in front of the Sri Relau Complex, heading towards Komtar, as well as the left lane of Jalan Dato Ismail Hashim, starting from shop lots near SJK © Min Sin to the Penang Golf Club heading towards Komtar. “In addition, the left lane at the traffic light intersection of Jalan Dato Ismail Hashim and Jalan Tun Dr Awang heading towards Komtar, as well as the leftmost lane on Jalan Tun Dr Awang, near the Taman Melati Jaya residential area heading towards Bayan Lepas, will also be closed, while other lanes will remain open to traffic,” it said in a statement today.

items.title: Law minister: Government considering review of Official Secrets Act, ready to table the AG-PP bill in Parliament
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 18 — The government may consider reviewing the Official Secrets Act (OSA) as part of a slew of reforms that it is currently pushing, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said today. Azalina said the law, dating back to 1972, would need to be updated so that it stays relevant with time. However, she said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim would have to determine when the bill should be brought to the Dewan Rakyat.

items.title: Ex-PM Muhyiddin’s trial: PMO gave names of contractors for Jana Wibawa projects, Finance Ministry officer says
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 18 — The Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) during the Muhyiddin administration had proposed contractors that passed the Finance Ministry’s evaluations and eventually won multi-million ringgit government projects under the Bumiputera contractors’ programme Jana Wibawa, a senior Finance Ministry (MOF) officer told the High Court today. Rosni today said she chaired an MOF committee that evaluated whether contractors were qualified for Jana Wibawa projects. Rosni said her committee had evaluated these contractors for Jana Wibawa projects after receiving their names from the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), stressing that the committee would not have evaluated these companies if the PMO did not propose them.

items.title: Anwar: Tabung Haji probes stretch beyond RCI, enforcement ordered to act fast, firm, fearless
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 18 — Investigations and actions by authorities regarding Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) issues may go beyond the scope and period examined by the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI), said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar, who is also the finance minister, said the RCI is the basis or “parent” for the investigation and scrutiny regarding the issue and there is no obstacle for the authorities to examine matters that occurred before or after the period involved. Earlier, Anwar in his closing speech ordered that follow-up actions regarding the TH issue be implemented firmly and immediately.

items.title: Budget 2027 to heed rakyat’s voices, PM Anwar says, as energy crisis weighs on households
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 18 — Budget 2027 must heed the voice of the people and meet their aspirations by driving the country’s development and improving the people’s well-being, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. “Therefore, the Madani government expresses its appreciation to everyone who contributed their views in the 2027 Budget Engagement Session. The 2027 Budget Engagement Session, chaired by Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, served as a prelude to the journey towards the Fifth Madani Budget, which will be tabled in Parliament on Oct 9, 2026.

items.title: Vivy Yusof, husband face CBT trial as court hears RM19.5m Khazanah transfers, director records
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 18 — The Sessions Court today was told that Khazanah Nasional Berhad (Khazanah) made two transfers totalling approximately RM19.5 million into an account belonging to local fashion company Fashion Valet Sdn Bhd in March 2018. CIMB Bank Berhad, Menara KL Sentral branch manager Lee Hui Nee, 58, said a review of Khazanah’s CIMB account statements revealed that the first transfer of RM7,848,000 was recorded on March 23, 2018, while the second transfer for RM11,742,000 was made on March 26, 2018. Both payments were made via interbank transfers from Khazanah’s CIMB account to Fashion Valet Sdn Bhd’s Public Bank account,” she said.

items.title: Kampar leads Malaysia in ageing population: 12.6pc of population aged 65 and above by 2025
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 18 — Kampar has the highest proportion of older citizens in Malaysia, with 12.6 per cent of its population aged 65 and above in 2025, according to the National Population and Family Development Board (LPPKN). According to The Star, LPPKN deputy chairman Juwairiya Zulkifli said the figure surpasses both the national average of 8 per cent and Perak’s overall proportion of 10.2 per cent, underscoring ageing as a major demographic challenge for the district. She said Kampar’s ageing trend stems from improved life expectancy and demographic shifts, including the migration of younger residents to urban centres such as Kuala Lumpur, Selangor and Penang for work, leaving older parents behind.

items.title: Temerloh fuel tanker crash: Driver charged with reckless driving causing deaths of mother, child
items.summary: TEMERLOH, Aug 18 — A tanker lorry driver today pleaded not guilty at the Magistrate’s Court here to two counts of reckless driving that caused the deaths of a mother and her son at KM9 of Jalan Temerloh-Triang here last Friday. He was charged with driving the tanker dangerously, causing the deaths of Nur Fatima Syuhada Abdullah, 39, and Muhamad Fattah Aisy Nuafal Saifulnizam, 12, at about 4pm on Aug 14. Last Friday, Nur Fatima Syuhada and Muhamad Fattah Aisy Nuafal were found burnt to death inside a car that caught fire after being crushed by a tanker lorry carrying 32,000 litres of fuel.

items.title: Loke assures RTS Link travellers: Passports accepted, QR system offered as digital option
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 18 — Passengers travelling on the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link can still use their regular passports for immigration clearance, while QR codes are available as an alternative through the digital system. Transport Minister Anthony Loke said the use of QR codes was not the only clearance method available to travellers at the Customs, Immigration and Quarantine (CIQ) Complex at the RTS Link Bukit Chagar. So, the QR code is an option available to travellers, but they can also use their regular passports,” he told reporters after a media visit to the RTS Link project at the RTS Link Bukit Chagar Station here today.

items.title: Prosecution appeals Zizie Izette’s acquittal in RM2.8m corruption case tied to Felcra unit trust
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 18 — The prosecution has filed a notice of appeal against the Sessions Court’s decision to acquit and discharge actress Datin Seri Zizie Izette Abdul Samad on three charges of abetting in a RM2.8 million corruption case involving a RM150 million investment in Public Mutual Berhad unit trusts, 11 years ago. Zizie Izette’s lawyer Ridha Abdah Subri confirmed the matter when contacted. Zizie Izette, 47, was freed of three amended charges under Section 28(1)(c) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act 2009.

items.title: Two‑minute Genting goldsmith heist: Suspects armed with axes escape in BMW with RM1.74m haul
items.summary: Acting Pahang police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said police received a report on the incident at 11.39am from a private security guard. He said preliminary investigations found that three male suspects wearing face masks, caps, and jackets entered the premises and took five trays of jewellery. Azry Akmar said police are continuing investigations to track down all three suspects.

items.title: Gobind pushes PM on equal MP allocations, calls for legislation to lock in fairness
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 18 — DAP today reiterated its call for the government to honour Pakatan Harapan’s election pledge of equal Constituency Development Funds (CDF) for all Members of Parliament. Gobind welcomed the Prime Minister’s recent announcement of additional direct funds for constituencies but said the move did not resolve the core issue. “I therefore urge the Prime Minister to address the delay and move forward with first providing all MPs with equal allocations, and subsequently enacting legislation that permanently secures equal constituency allocations for every MP in Malaysia,” he said.

items.title: Malaysia and Singapore to announce RTS Link fare soon, Loke says talks moving smoothly
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 18 — An official announcement on the fare for the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link service will be made jointly by the Transport Ministries (MOT) of both countries in the near future. He said this when asked whether the RTS Link fare had been finalised. Loke said RTS Operations Pte Ltd (RTSO) was now at the final stage of discussions with the Malaysian and Singaporean governments to finalise the fare and payment mechanism for the RTS Link.

items.title: SPM 2026 written exams set November 23 to December 17, oral and practical earlier
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 18 — The 2026 Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) written examination will be held from November 23 to December 17, the Ministry of Education (MOE) said today. In a statement today, the ministry said the Bahasa Melayu Oral Test and English Language Oral Test will be held from October 26 to 29 and November 2 to 5, respectively. The Science Practical Test will take place from November 16 to 18, followed by the Bahasa Melayu Listening Test on November 30 and the English Language Listening Test on December 1.

items.title: Transport Ministry greenlights RM60m bridge, giving Komuter passengers direct access to RTS station
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 18 — The government will build a bridge between the Bukit Chagar RTS Link Station and KTMB Komuter service to strengthen public transport integration and facilitate passenger access to the transit system. We want to encourage RTS Link users to take public transport to reach Bukit Chagar or to exit from Bukit Chagar,” he told reporters after a visit to the RTS Link project at Bukit Chagar here today. He said the Bukit Chagar RTS Link Station will also be integrated with JB Sentral, e-hailing services and other public transport, making it a multi-modal public transport hub.

items.title: Anwar resists GST comeback, eyes selective levy fixes to reinforce SST ahead of Budget 2027
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 18 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today again indicated his hesitation to reintroduce the Goods and Services Tax during a dialogue with businesses and ministries ahead of the tabling of Budget 2027, slated for October. But Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, suggested that he is open to incorporating some “elements” of the consumption levy, if it helps improve the Sales and Services Tax. GST is a ‘broad-based tax’, we tax all the people, and I disagree with that.”

items.title: Public Works Ministry spends entire RM2b road maintenance allocation, to seek more funds
items.summary: SEBERANG PERAI, Aug 18 — The Works Ministry has fully used its roughly RM2 billion allocation for road maintenance and aims to seek more allocation, Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Maslan said today. “Hopefully, road maintenance allocations can be increased,” he said. “Road maintenance accounts for only 13 per cent,” he said.

items.title: Ahmad Maslan: Umno’s state election moves are strategy, not ‘backstabbing’ of Unity Government partners
items.summary: He said Umno and Pakatan Harapan (PH) did not have state-level agreements in Johor, Negeri Sembilan and Melaka, unlike in Penang, where he said there was an agreement. he said. he said.

items.title: Home minister: Drone surveillance boosts AADK drug enforcement, identifies 23,317 suspects
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 18 — The National Anti-Drug Agency (AADK) has identified 23,317 suspected drug addicts through surveillance by its fleet of 18 drones, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said today. He said the drones had enhanced AADK’s enforcement capabilities by allowing the agency to monitor drug hotspots around the clock, including through night flights. Saifuddin said information gathered through drone surveillance was channelled to AADK’s operations room, where it was analysed and used to guide enforcement action.

items.title: Fahmi: Facebook commits ‘most sins’ against Malaysians with online gambling, scams
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 18 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil today took a swipe at Facebook, describing the platform as the “most guilty” among social media platforms when it comes to enabling online gambling and scams in Malaysia. Fahmi said Facebook accounted for 78 per cent of online gambling content identified by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) for removal between January 1 and August 17 this year. Fahmi said MCMC had sought the removal of 470,593 pieces of harmful content between January 1 and August 17, with platforms complying with 93 per cent of the requests, involving 436,661 pieces of content.
